content.rationale: The requirement sentences with a runnable artifact dependent: conformance is what running the artifact shows, so the gate states the observables the sentences demand and leaves the verdict to the run. The interaction must also apply each state change incrementally per stppxysx — a selection, hover, drag or keyboard focus change looks up the elements the change affects by the identity it carries and writes only those, and the changes pending within a frame are merged into at most one application to the surface, carrying the last pending value rather than dropping it. The check draws its own surface from the layout the interaction asks its delegate for, using only the page interface's identity attributes and the layout module (ympqvvwr, qmsmvrnr), so it runs at this node's base with no renderer in the graph; the real-renderer integration stays with ylolxwpv. It drives real pointer and key events and observes, per change, every element lookup the interaction makes on the surface or on anything the surface contains — any of querySelector, querySelectorAll, getElementsByClassName and getElementsByTagName, with any selector, so naming no selector cannot hide the read — together with the class writes it asks of each drawn element and the relayout calls it makes for one drag within a frame. The check also drives pointer gestures the way a browser delivers them: a press lands on the element under the pointer, the release and the rest of that gesture are addressed where the surface's document was asked to send them (pointer capture when the gesture takes it, the element under the pointer otherwise), and the compatibility event a repeated press produces is addressed to the nearest common inclusive ancestor of the two clicks' targets. The check therefore also spans a graph reload (uvmutyww): the renderer draws the new revision in elements of its own and the page hands the interaction the new graph through the page interface's graph swap, so the two clicks of one double click no longer share the pressed element and the compatibility event lands on the surface whoever is capturing — an addressing the gesture's own capture choice cannot move back onto the pressed node, which is why the check cannot be satisfied by fulfilling the requirement through keeping the browser's addressing where it started. Read back through the delegate's request to open a node's document and through the selection it reports, the check observes that a gesture acts on the subject its press landed on — a node, an edge or the empty canvas — unchanged for the whole gesture, and that each gesture's subject is its own.
